youtube.title: Why Soda Bottle Caps Have Tiny Slits 🥤 #Shorts #science #facts #didyouknow
youtube.description:
Those small slits cut across the threads of a plastic soda bottle cap are vent slots. A carbonated drink holds gas under pressure, and if the cap sealed the whole way up the thread, that pressure would still be trapped as you unscrewed it, so the cap could shoot off. The slots let the gas hiss out first while the threads still grip the cap, so it comes off safely.

Subscribe to The Hidden Why for a new why every day.

#Shorts #science #facts #thehiddenwhy

sources: Closure makers' notes: vent slots in PCO bottle-cap threads release pressure before the cap disengages
Packaging engineering: venting prevents caps launching ('missile effect') on carbonated bottles
